name: phase3_vnni_sparsity
description: Does the int8 dot-product compute draw differently when more of its input
is zero -- i.e. is activation sparsity visible through the MAC array, on top
of the load-movement channel phase3_sparsity already measures? This is Phase
3 item 2, the quantised-inference angle, and it is the freshest one: vpdpbusd
(AVX-VNNI) is exactly the instruction ONNX/PyTorch int8 inference issues on
this part, and Phase 1 found it leaks +0.20 W register-resident, so there is
a plausible compute channel distinct from movement.
Two victims measured in one session so they can be read paired:
ws_sparse_op_vnni  -- sparse activation stream + 8 vpdpbusd per iteration
ws_sparse_op_mov   -- the identical sparse stream + 8 vmovdqa (no compute)
The load stream, addresses and op count are identical across densities AND
across the two victims, so work_balance holds and vnni - mov at a fixed
density is the compute channel with the movement channel differenced out --
the same paired reading the instruction table uses against loads_only.
Selector: low 16 bits = nonzero words per 1024, high 32 bits = 0 -> the
default all-ones activation pattern (max magnitude, max SNR for this first
pass; vpdpbusd treats operand a as unsigned and b as signed, and both
sources are the same loaded word, so 0xFF bytes give products of 255*-1 and
the per-burst accumulator stays well inside int32 -- this is exactly the
all-ones case ws_op_vnni already runs in the instruction table). A follow-up
can set a small realistic int8 pattern (e.g. 0x03030303) and a fixed dense
weight via the high bits without any code change.
Densities are trimmed to six against the doubled victim count. Density 0 is
the A/A gate for both victims; density 1024 (all nonzero) anchors vnni to
the instruction table's ws_op_vnni (+2.109 W) and mov to loads_only.
Read per run for the gates, then analysis.aggregate --against the mov row
per density, or the sparsity analysis with the compute-channel option (see
summary.cmd). Expect the movement channel (both victims) to rise steeply
with density; the open question is whether vnni sits measurably above mov,
and whether that gap itself grows with density.
